messages:
jenna_customer: Hey team — AcmeCorp on Private/VPC is hitting intermittent outbound failures to the hosted API. Started ~10:15 UTC. Symptoms: app logs show TLS handshake errors, and their bastion curl sometimes returns a 502. Example from their bastion:

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat 
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (198.51.100.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
curl: (35) SSL receive error
```

App log snippet: 
``n502 Bad Gateway: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
```

They're in on-prem air-gapped mode with a corporate outbound proxy + split-tunnel. Customer reports it only fails for our domains; other external HTTPS calls succeed. Escalating to network and devex — can someone take point? cc @sarah_support @mike_netops

sarah_support: Thanks @jenna_customer — can you confirm the exact bastion command and whether they set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars? Also need the output of:

```bash
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts
```

If the proxy is doing TLS inspection it usually shows up there (re-signed cert). Any chance the proxy inserts a corporate CA?

mike_netops: pinging the network team — quick checklist:
- Are they doing SNI or IP-based split-tunnel? if proxy terminates TLS we will see a private CA in s_client output.
- If split-tunnel sends redwood traffic via corp proxy, maybe the proxy rewrites SNI/Host.
- Need tcpdump on the bastion for a failing request (capture first 1000 bytes) and the proxy access logs for that minute.

Can the customer run a tcpdump: 

```bash
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host api.redwood-inference.com -s 0 -w /tmp/redwood-tcpdump.pcap
# then reproduce the curl once or twice and upload pcap
```

kai_devex: I bumped into a similar case last month — corporate TLS inspection re-signs the cert and some clients (golang default TLS stack) reject it because the CA isn't in the system trust store or because the proxy rewrites SNI. Workarounds to repro quickly:
- Run curl with --proxy (explicit) vs no proxy to see difference.
- Try: `curl -v --proxy <proxy:port> https://api.redwood-inference.com` and `curl -v --noproxy '*' https://api.redwood-inference.com` to confirm proxy involvement.
- If s_client shows a corporate cert, ask the customer to import that CA into the bastion's OS-level trust store (or into the language runtime store).

jenna_customer: They set HTTPS_PROXY to http://corp-proxy.local:8080. Trying the --noproxy toggle now. One quick paste from s_client shows: 'subject=/CN=Corp-Intercept-Proxy' instead of api.redwood-inference.com — so looks like TLS inspect. They say they cannot add CA to the system store without change control.

sarah_support: OK that matches TLS-inspection. Two plausible failure modes here: 
1) The proxy re-signs certs but the app/container doesn't trust the corp CA -> CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED/handshake fail.
2) Proxy rewrites SNI/Host header and our routing/ALB sees unexpected hostname -> upstream 502 in their app stack.

Short-term mitigation: if they can noproxy the traffic for our endpoints (split-tunnel config), that will restore end-to-end TLS. Longer-term: either import corp CA into trust store or configure proxy to do SNI passthrough for our domains.

mike_netops: Also confirm the proxy doesn't alter TLS client hello version/cipher list. Some older proxies downgrade TLS causing ssl3_get_record errors. If they can't change CA trust store we can provide them with an allowlist of egress IPs and FQDNs so netops can create an explicit bypass for those destinations.

deploy-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-2443 (customer: AcmeCorp) assigned to sarah_support, mike_netops — priority P2.

kai_devex: Repro steps I'm asking the customer to try (safe, low-risk):
1) From bastion: `curl -v --noproxy api.redwood-inference.com https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat`
2) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com` and copy the certificate chain.
3) If (1) succeeds and (2) shows corporate cert, ask their infra to add an outbound bypass rule for `api.redwood-inference.com` (or our IP ranges).

jenna_customer: Confirmed: `--noproxy` call succeeds (200). When proxied, curl shows the corp CN. They opened a SOC change to add an allowlist entry for our domain. They're asking if we can provide a recommended egress IP list and the list of hostnames to add.

sarah_support: I'll pull the documented egress IP ranges and hostname list and paste here — also note that for Private deployments the customer can request dedicated egress IPs if needed (helps allowlisting). Action items: 
- sarah_support: provide egress IP ranges + public FQDN list in the thread (ETA 30m).
- mike_netops: help review their proxy logs if allowlist change doesn't fix (ETA 2h).
- kai_devex: provide guidance on trust store import steps for common distros (ETA 2h).

mike_netops: Quick note for debugging if the allowlist still fails: capture the proxy access log and check Host and SNI fields, and also confirm that proxy honors CONNECT method (some proxies downgrade CONNECT into a new TLS session which causes hostname mismatch).

jenna_customer: Thanks — customer applied allowlist for api.redwood-inference.com and reported success after 15 minutes. Will keep monitoring and call back if flaky. :thumbsup:

sarah_support: Great, closing for now but keeping incident open to verify 24h stability. Marking follow-up to offer dedicated egress IPs for AcmeCorp if they want more stable production setup. :white_check_mark:
